thread_analysis.thread_summary: IDEAL company (Satoru Sanada) engages Allion across a long single continuous thread covering multiple stages of a Bluetooth SIG registration: scope clarification (optional accessory exclusion), fee/payment mechanics (exchange rate timing, wire transfer delegation pros/cons, Invoice/Qualification Number assignment for third-party payment), Step 3 documentation (antenna datasheet substitution), and final registration steps (component test exemption, Review Page, Compliance Folder document collection).
all_questions_found: Does an optional Bluetooth-unrelated resin cover/case accessory need to be included in registration scope?
When is the exchange rate determined for a USD-denominated Declaration Fee wire transfer?
Can the Step 3 antenna datasheet be a copy of the relevant page from the BLE module's own spec sheet?
What are the pros and cons of delegating the Declaration Fee wire transfer to Allion versus self-transfer?
If a different company will actually wire the registration fee, who gets the Qualification Number and how does the Invoice process work?
Is a test sample submission required if the relevant components already passed prior testing?
thread_analysis.key_technical_discussion: Registration scope excludes Bluetooth-unrelated accessories; USD fee exchange rates are fixed to the TTS rate as of the month-end prior to quotation issuance, not the payment date; antenna datasheet requirements can be satisfied by a BLE module spec sheet excerpt containing radiation gain characteristics; Declaration Fee wire transfer can be self-executed or delegated to Allion (+¥100,000, ~3 weeks) depending on the customer's USD transfer capability and invoicing needs; Qualification Number assignment follows whichever company's account generated the Invoice, regardless of who actually pays; pre-existing passing test results exempt customers from new test sample submission.
thread_analysis.key_decision_logic: Each procedural question is resolved by matching the specific requirement's underlying purpose (Bluetooth relevance, technical content presence, payment capability, account ownership, prior test validity) rather than applying a blanket rule, allowing flexible but consistent application across a long multi-stage engagement.
thread_analysis.risk_if_done_wrong: Misapplying any of these procedural rules (scope, exchange rate timing, document substitution, payment delegation, Invoice/Qualification Number assignment, test sample exemption) could create unnecessary cost, delay, or registration ownership confusion for the customer.
thread_analysis.consulting_mistake: None identified — Allion provided accurate, consistent answers to each distinct procedural question across this extended engagement.
thread_analysis.consulting_takeaway: Long single-customer threads often contain many small but genuinely distinct procedural questions spanning different registration stages (scope, payment, documentation, final steps); each should be extracted as its own case rather than merged, since they address different rules and would otherwise be hard to retrieve individually.
